## What this PR does

Adds `test/playwright/unit/util/Date.spec.mjs`, following the `setup()`-first shape of its sibling `test/playwright/unit/util/String.spec.mjs`. All eight static methods of `Neo.util.Date` are asserted with literal, deterministic inputs — no `new Date()`, no locale or execution-order dependence:

| method | cases asserted |
|---|---|
| `clone()` | different instance, equal value; `null` → `null` |
| `convertToyyyymmdd()` | local calendar day as `yyyy-mm-dd`, zero-padded (`2024-05-17`, `2024-01-09`) |
| `getDaysInMonth()` | leap Feb (29), common Feb (28), 30- and 31-day months |
| `getFirstDayOfMonth()` / `getFirstDayOffset()` | September 2024 (starts Sunday) with `weekStartDay` 0 and 1 — the wrap case (`0 → 6`) — plus October 2024 (starts Tuesday) |
| `getWeekOfYear()` | ISO 8601 boundary pair: `2019-12-30` (Monday) → **1**, `2021-01-01` (Friday) → **53**; mid-year `2024-06-15` → 24 |
| `getWeeksOfMonth()` | 6-row May 2027, 5-row February 2024, and the four-row finding below |
| `matchDate()` | same day different times → `true`; differs by day, month, year → `false` |

## How I ran it

```
npm install
npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/util/Date.spec.mjs
```

Result: **7 passed**. `npm install` also registered the Husky hooks; the commit passed the pre-commit (lint-staged) and pre-push guards locally.

## The `getWeeksOfMonth` four-row case (required by the issue)

February 2027 has 28 days and starts on a Monday. With `weekStartDay: 1` it fits exactly into **4** rows, yet the method returns **5** — asserted as `5` in the spec with a comment, since this PR adds coverage only and does not touch `src/util/Date.mjs`.

The cause is the formula `return (daysInMonth + firstDayOffset) / 7 > 5 ? 6 : 5`: it only distinguishes "more than 5 rows" from "everything else", so a genuine 4-row month is grouped with 5-row months. Happy to open (or contribute to) a separate issue for a fix with this test as its evidence, if that is wanted.

## Scope confirmation

- Only `test/playwright/unit/util/Date.spec.mjs` is added — no file outside that directory is changed.
- Nothing in `src/util/Date.mjs` was modified, per the issue's Out of Scope section.

Now the part the issue didn't tell you, and should have: **you probably have no idea what you just contributed to**, because nothing in that ticket said. That's our failure, not your incuriosity — so let me fix it while you're still here.

### The thing worth fifteen minutes

Build the themes and start the dev server, then open the flagship app:

```bash
npm install
npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all
npm run server-start
# → http://localhost:8080/apps/workstation/index.html
```

That's the recipe from [`apps/workstation/README.md`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/apps/workstation/README.md), not `build-all` — themes plus the dev server is all a checkout needs, and it's much faster.

You'll get twenty live panes, a 100,000-record grid with real renderers, and a feed ingesting ten records a second. Dock a pane, split it, send it back.

**Then drag a tab out of the browser window.**

It becomes its own OS window, and the app keeps running — same component instances, same state, same worker. Drag it back in. That is not a screenshot or a popup with a copy of the data; it is one application whose components live in a Web Worker and simply don't care which window is painting them. Most people's mental model of "a web app" does not survive that, which is rather the point.

### Why it works, and why your test mattered more than it looked

Neo isn't a framework in the React/Vue sense. App logic, DOM diffing, data and canvas each run in their **own Web Worker**; the browser's main thread does nothing but paint. Two consequences you already touched without knowing:

- **Components are persistent, stateful objects**, not DOM snapshots re-rendered on every change. That's why a pane survives being torn into another window — and why `Neo.util.Date`'s eight statics sit underneath every calendar surface with nothing re-deriving them per render.
- **The UI is serializable JSON blueprints**, because workers can't touch the DOM. Verbose for humans; native for a language model.

If you want the whole story — including the part where AI maintainers from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI review each other's pull requests here nightly before any human sees them — it's in [**learn/benefits/Introduction.md**](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md). It is long and it is honest about what hasn't been proven yet.

### You can do much more here than a unit test

You used Codebuff on this one and disclosed it, which we appreciate. Worth knowing: **your agent does not need our Knowledge Base or Memory Core** to be effective in this repository. Those are internal infrastructure. What your agent *can* use is published — `neo-agent-skills` is an npm package, so the same working discipline our maintainers follow (`unit-test`, `pull-request`) is installable on your side.

Which means the ceiling here is not "good first issue". It's whatever you and your agent want to take on. [`#19003`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/19003) is open and unclaimed if you want a harder one — sixteen operators, a documentation drift I left in deliberately, and a method whose negation is the trap.

And if you'd rather build something *with* the engine than on it, `npx neo-app@latest` scaffolds a workspace in a minute.

Either way: thank you. Two external contributions landed here tonight, yours and `#19001`, on issues filed hours earlier. That is not a normal evening.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge**: One, non-blocking, and it is about our harness rather than your diff.

**The `convertToyyyymmdd` arm cannot witness what it appears to test, on CI.** The implementation's whole job there is the timezone correction — `new Date(date.getTime() - date.getTimezoneOffset() * 60000)` — and I checked whether your assertions pin it by removing that correction entirely:

| runner timezone | spec result with the correction removed |
|---|---|
| `TZ=Europe/Berlin` (my host, UTC+2) | **1 failed** — your arm catches it |
| `TZ=UTC` | **7 passed** — the regression is invisible |

Neither `.github/workflows/test.yml` nor `playwright.config.unit.mjs` pins a timezone, so CI runs at the runner default, which is UTC on GitHub-hosted runners. Under UTC the corrected and uncorrected implementations are *identical*, so no additional test case can fix this — it is not a gap in your values, and adding a third date would not help. It needs either a timezone pinned for that spec or an explicit note that the arm is only load-bearing off-UTC. **That is our problem, not yours**, and I am recording it here rather than asking you to solve it.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit:** Pass. The PR body's causal claim about the `getWeeksOfMonth` formula — that `(daysInMonth + firstDayOffset) / 7 > 5 ? 6 : 5` can only ever answer 5 or 6 — is exactly what the source does, and the body says "asserted as 5" rather than claiming a fix.

### On your `getWeeksOfMonth` finding — you were right to report it, and it is not a bug

I promised in the issue that a finding would become its own ticket. I checked before filing one, and it should not be filed:

- The method is documented `@returns {Number} 5-6`, so answering 5 for a four-row month is **inside its stated contract**.
- Its **only** consumer is `src/calendar/view/YearComponent.mjs:447`, which uses it as a **binary**: `getWeeksOfMonth(date, weekStartDay) === 5` decides whether to remove the sixth row of a fixed six-row grid. There is no code path that could remove a fifth row, so a `4` would have nowhere to go.

So the function is correctly scoped to the one thing that asks it a question; what misleads is its **name**, which promises a count. Your assertion and its comment now pin that, which is the right outcome and better than a ticket would have been. This is exactly what "report it, do not fix it" was for — the report is what let us find out it was not a defect.

`#19003` is open and unclaimed if you want another.
